title: policy.json: merge
description: The basic local merge queue (design part 14): main is fast-forwarded only to a commit that passed the full suite as part of its batch.

mode.description: Who decides each merge. "queue": the orchestrator runs the queue whenever branches are waiting. "owner": finished branches wait for the owner, who names the ones to merge (hitld merge --only <branch>); the same rebase, fast checks, full suite and fast-forward then run. A new project starts in owner mode; the queue is opted into once the record supports it.

main_branch.description: The integration branch. Only the merge queue moves it.

batch_max.description: The most branches in one batch before the full suite runs. Smaller batches make bisection cheaper.

fast_checks.description: Commands run on each rebased branch before it joins the batch: lint, type check, the item's acceptance checks, the tests nearest its touches. Each runs through the shell in the queue's worktree with HITLD_ITEM, HITLD_TOUCHES and HITLD_CHANGED set. A failure sends the branch back to its executor.
fast_checks.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

full_suite.description: The full test suite, run once per batch on the combined result. With none, the queue refuses to move main, because it could not keep main green.
full_suite.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

generated.description: Generated files: never merged by hand. A rebase conflict confined to them takes the batch's version, and the regenerate command rebuilds them once per batch, before the full suite.

regenerate.description: The command that rebuilds them, run through the shell at the batch's root.
regenerate.x-hitld-executes: run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

flake_reruns.description: How many times a failing full suite is rerun on the same commit. A pass on a rerun does not merge: the batch is held, the failure is recorded as a flake candidate, and the owner decides (design 14.4 and 14.7).
